# Open-LM-EA9

Research and development toward comprehensive, modular Techart LM-EA9 firmware,
a documented host communication protocol, and a polished, easy-to-use macOS app.
The initial target is a Sony A7C II and manually adapted Contax C/Y lenses.

The **macOS prototype uses native SwiftUI/AppKit and Swift IOHID**, following the
system audit. All flashed firmware is C. The [updated working recommendation](docs/system-design-recommendation.md)
is to build on upstream C and defer Rust while qualifying A7C II compatibility.

An [eight-hour firmware hardening pass](docs/firmware-hardening-2026-10-15.md)
is running through 08:55 America/New_York on October 15. The first eleven Astra
lanes produced frozen [upstream C 3.3](firmware/candidates/3.3.0/README.md).
Follow-up audits now produce [3.6 offline](firmware/candidates/3.6.0/README.md):
a scoped startup EIC handoff prevents competing receive producers while keeping
UART reception active, retaining 3.5's target/time and 3.4's encoder/query fixes.
It retains the upstream C controller and aperture policy. Exact repeat builds,
production-path regressions with failing controls, independent composition and
compiled writer/stack checks, and all 53 Swift tests pass.
[Evidence and limitations](docs/evidence/upstream-36-handoff-2026-10-15.md).
The offline decoder also distinguishes inconsistent or partial multi-boot logs.
**3.6 is uploaded and strictly byte-verified, but camera capture/shutdown failed.
Further 3.6 camera trials are held.** The owner reports slight focus movement,
shutter-press freeze and shutdown nonresponse. A read-only backup preserved 13
valid diagnostic pages: a sticky `servo-wrong-way` inhibit and a later shutdown
UART-disable marker. This does not locate the shutter failure or prove camera
power-off. [Failure evidence](docs/evidence/upstream-36-camera-failure-2026-10-15.md).
The owner authorized the interactive installation after
[3.2 strict verification passed](docs/evidence/upstream-32-upload-2026-10-15.md).
No hardware was accessed during scheduled work; the separate
[3.6 installation record](docs/evidence/upstream-36-upload-2026-10-15.md)
tracks the owner-coordinated USB steps. Physical compatibility remains failed.
Earlier released images and original recovery remain exact.

The prototype includes all eight requested lens profiles, local metadata editing,
versioned JSON import/export, verified USB backup, and a staged application
upload/read-back path for lens metadata. The current app (0.19.1, build 24) refreshes
connection and local verification history automatically. Device shows product
photos, connection, dated firmware and the last verified lens, with a dropdown
to choose and apply another profile on firmware that supports runtime profiles.
Lens Library remains a secondary gallery/editor.
It marks installed 3.6 as held and disables ordinary installation of that image.
The upstream candidates use the original fixed 50mm profile; they cannot apply
runtime lens edits. [Factory reconstruction remains partial](docs/reverse-engineering/status-2026-10-15.md).
The **historical upstream C startup diagnostic 3.2 for Contax Zeiss 50mm f/1.4
was uploaded and strictly byte-verified after physical reconnect**. The owner
requested proceeding to 3.6 before a 3.2 camera cycle. It
repairs first-window opener loss reproduced in 11 frozen-3.1 cases, restores
stock lens ID 234 as a compatibility control and
adds bounded startup/handshake records in a reserved application tail. It retains
upstream's AF algorithms and optional aperture-field behavior. All 12 repaired
arrival cases, eight upstream host outcomes, nine compiled ARM writer checks,
seven decoder tests and 53 Swift tests pass. It is **not camera-qualified**;
the A7C II aperture/capture behavior remains unverified for that image.
The upload retained fresh backup, durable journal and physical-reconnect guards.
[Current installation and test record](docs/evidence/upstream-32-upload-2026-10-15.md).
[Candidate](firmware/candidates/3.2.0/README.md) ·
[Implementation/evidence](docs/evidence/upstream-32-startup-diagnostic-2026-10-15.md) ·
[One-cycle and log-retrieval procedure](docs/upstream-startup-diagnostic-test.md).

The **direct upstream 3.1 baseline for Contax Zeiss 50mm f/1.4 is uploaded and
strictly byte-verified after physical reconnect**. **Camera acceptance failed:**
the owner reports aperture `--`, no shutter release and no motor movement;
normal shutdown is confirmed. Further 3.1 trials are held. It builds the
current pinned upstream commit `d52ed06`, preserving its controller, protocol,
main loop, homing/park and driver C implementations. Only build compatibility,
version/lens constants and corresponding pupil-row configuration differ.
Both upstream host builds pass; all 53 Swift tests pass. App 0.14/build 17 and
the explicit native `apply-upstream` path retain fresh backup/journal/reconnect/
strict verification guards. This comparison is fixed to the original 50mm
f/1.4 profile; runtime lens edits cannot change its compiled firmware. A fresh
two-pass backup matched the previous verified AF 3.0 flash exactly. All 320 pages
were acknowledged; no post-START read was sent on the armed connection.
Fresh two-pass readback and a separate offline audit matched the full fixed
image/metadata and unchanged protected flash/factory data. Actual focus mode and
other settings remain unverified; motor silence alone does not prove an AF fault.
App 0.14.1 marks the image as held and disables ordinary baseline installation.
[Failure and five-case startup investigation](docs/evidence/upstream-31-camera-failure-2026-10-14.md) ·
[Installation record](docs/evidence/upstream-31-upload-2026-10-14.md) ·
[Baseline provenance and limits](docs/evidence/upstream-baseline-2026-10-14.md) ·
[Candidate](firmware/candidates/3.1.0/README.md) ·
[Upload/camera procedure](docs/upstream-baseline-test.md).

The previous **AF 3.0 candidate for Contax Zeiss 50mm f/1.4 was uploaded and
strictly byte-verified after physical reconnect**. Fresh two-pass backup/readback and
separate offline audits passed. **Camera acceptance failed:** the owner reports
half-press focusing followed by full-press freeze, no saved photo and battery-
required recovery. Further AF 3.0 trials are held.
[Failure and new factory comparison](docs/evidence/af-30-camera-failure-2026-10-14.md).
[October 14 installation record](docs/evidence/af-30-upload-2026-10-14.md).
The candidate was prepared offline,
with factory-derived capture interlocks/raw opener echo, priority shutdown
without new motion, and nonblocking bounded reference acquisition. Cancelled
homing needs a fresh motion command to retry, within a two-attempt per-boot
budget; faults remain sticky. The October 13 preparation pass used no hardware;
the separately authorized October 14 upload is recorded above.
[Implementation, factory evidence and limits](docs/evidence/af-30-candidate-2026-10-13.md).
[Candidate and exact pins](firmware/candidates/3.0.0/README.md).
25 new arbitration/readiness cases and 40 retained link cases pass; exact frozen
controls detect 8 AF 2.9 and 15 AF 2.8 defects. All 51 Swift tests, the full
firmware suite and retained original-instruction comparisons pass. The signed
app/CLI produce the same personalized image as Python. It has 392 bytes of
flash margin, 2,380 bytes static RAM and 8 KiB reserved stack, with high-water
and physical timing unmeasured. Older images and original recovery stay exact.

Historical **AF 2.9 camera acceptance failed and further trials are held**.
On that image, the owner reports focus followed by capture freeze
requiring battery removal, then reset movement with no later focus movement;
shutdown worked on the latter reboot. The actual focus mode/reference state
remain unknown. Software fixes do not prove the physical cause or factory
parity. AF 3.0 also failed capture. New finite original-instruction replay exposes a
phase-driven interruption/raw-echo divergence for five tested non-`0x0a` IDs;
the physical cause is not proven. No replacement firmware was built by this
investigation and no more AF 3.0 camera trials are requested.
[AF 2.9 failure record](docs/evidence/af-29-camera-failure-2026-10-12.md).
[AF 2.9 installation](docs/evidence/af-29-upload-2026-10-12.md).

The historical **AF 2.8 candidate is uploaded and strictly byte-verified after physical
reconnect**, but **camera acceptance failed**: the owner reports frozen preview,
poor focus response, darker exposure and a later shutdown hang requiring battery
removal. Further 2.8 trials are suspended. **Original stock 1.8 was subsequently restored
and strictly byte-verified after physical reconnect**, with a separate readback
audit. All 128 KiB match the stock snapshot immediately before AF 2.8 installation.
[Recovery record before AF 2.9 installation](docs/evidence/stock-18-af28-recovery-2026-10-12.md).
See [the camera failure record](docs/evidence/af-28-camera-failure-2026-10-12.md).
The software milestone was prepared and tested offline. A pure measured-motion
observer now preserves coast/reversal after command completion, requires a fresh
quiet interval before reporting rest, and discards stale per-frame history.
It follows REA's factory frame-sync behavior by reporting the same measured
position in both fields. Fixed aperture/opaque `0x34`, factory control law,
drivers and completion policy remain unchanged. See
[implementation, tests and limits](docs/evidence/af-28-motion-telemetry-2026-10-12.md).
The [October 12 native upload](docs/evidence/af-28-upload-2026-10-12.md)
completed with a fresh two-pass backup; no post-START read was sent. Subsequent
two-pass readback and a separate offline evidence audit matched the complete
candidate/profile and protected flash/factory data. The displayed f/1.4 is an
owner observation; it does not qualify exposure or AF. Older images and stock recovery are preserved. Sensor noise, physical settling, exposure and optical AF remain
unqualified; factory reconstruction remains partial. The candidate has 400 bytes
of flash headroom and uses 2,200 bytes of static RAM.
The app displays **Actual aperture: Unknown** separately from its fixed camera
f-number; the lens ring still controls the physical iris. The historical **AF 2.4
factory baseline** replaces the upstream controller with independently implemented
stock speed/PID/callback/completion semantics. Its pure controller passes 7,323
original-instruction comparisons. Its authorized upload and strict two-pass
USB verification passed, including an independent audit. **Its first owner
focus attempt failed**, with motor movement but no focus/photo release, a dark
view and no shown f-number in P/A. Further 2.4 camera tests are suspended.
Actual focus mode and exposure settings remain unverified. The unchanged
controller also reproduces small-correction and full-travel session faults in
the inherited mechanical simulator; these are readiness gaps, not a proven
hardware diagnosis. See [the failure investigation](docs/evidence/af-24-camera-failure-2026-10-11.md)
and [the baseline design](docs/reverse-engineering/factory-af-baseline.md).
AF 2.3 hardens received frames, command snapshots, Stop handling, bounded query
processing and startup waits. It was byte-verified after physical USB-cap
reconnect. With the 50mm lens and C/Y-to-M converter, the owner reports eventual
focus and substantial hunting; sharpness, actual AF settings and loaded shutdown
remain unverified. Original same-unit stock **1.8.0 was restored for comparison** and its full
application slot matched the original backup; the owner reported much less
hunting. After the failed AF 2.4 attempt, the original stock 1.8 application
has been restored again and **strictly byte-verified after physical reconnect**,
with an independent audit. The owner reports stock AUTO overexposure and a
selectable P-mode aperture, widest f/2, then one-stop overexposure at physical
f/1.4 / camera f/2. The reported exposure failure is accepted; the photo was
not retained and does not block firmware investigation. Exact cause, lifecycle
and controlled AF-S remain unqualified. [Historical stock exposure record](docs/evidence/stock-18-af24-recovery-2026-10-11.md).
During the earlier stock comparison, camera use before readback changed 13 stock saved-motion bytes, causing strict
verification to fail. A later explicit reviewed resolution matched a fresh
backup to that audit and archived the failure without relabeling it a strict
pass; bootloader and factory data remain exact. [AF 2.4 installation and
reconnect progress](docs/evidence/af-24-upload-2026-10-11.md) is recorded separately;
comparison settings from the earlier stock report remain unknown.
AF 2.1 and 2.2 were previously byte-verified, with 2.1 owner reports of
motor movement and proper shutdown. For 2.2, the owner reports normal camera
startup, no observed startup movement without input, quiet idle and normal motor
shutdown. Homing and measured timing remain unverified. The converter is now
available for a controlled loaded-lens baseline.
The Biotar is 58mm f/2, as confirmed by the owner. For current offline firmware
reproduction, first follow the pinned toolchain and exact 3.5 source prerequisites
in the [3.6 workbench](firmware/upstream-hardening/next36/README.md). Existing
materializations are preserved; choose fresh private output paths:

```sh
python3 scripts/build-upstream-handoff.py --output artifacts/private/recheck36
python3 scripts/test-upstream-handoff.py --build artifacts/private/recheck36 --output artifacts/private/recheck36-tests
./scripts/swift-local.sh test
./scripts/build-macos-app.sh
```

The earlier `build-firmware.py` and `build-upstream-baseline.py` reproduce/check
historical metadata/custom firmware and 3.1 respectively; they do not build 3.6.
On a fresh checkout, restore the ignored photographed assets as described in
[photo provenance](references/visuals/README.md) before packaging the app.
For interactive app use, open `dist/Open LM-EA9.app` after the build. Keep it
closed during CLI USB operations and offline runs; normal app refresh enumerates
connected devices. Building or passing tests does not authorize a flash.

# Firmware development

The latest candidate is [upstream AF 3.6](candidates/3.6.0/README.md), prepared
offline for the original Contax Zeiss 50mm f/1.4. It builds on pinned upstream C
with reviewed framing, ownership, homing, query, target/time and startup fixes;
the controller, optical maps and aperture policy remain upstream. Exact repeat
builds and production-path regressions pass, with physical camera qualification
still open. See [3.6 evidence](../docs/evidence/upstream-36-handoff-2026-10-15.md)
and the [build/test workbench](upstream-hardening/next36/README.md) for prerequisites
and commands. App 0.19.1/build 24 marks 3.6 held after the
[reported capture/shutdown failure](../docs/evidence/upstream-36-camera-failure-2026-10-15.md)
and disables ordinary installation. Preserve the original image for research;
do not repeat camera testing of 3.6.

**Hardware gate:** [3.2 strict verification passed](../docs/evidence/upstream-32-upload-2026-10-15.md)
after owner-confirmed physical reconnect. The separately authorized
[3.6 upload and strict verification passed](../docs/evidence/upstream-36-upload-2026-10-15.md)
after its own physical reconnect. The later camera cycle failed, and a read-only
backup/log review was completed. The
[coordinated camera and log procedure](../docs/upstream-handoff-test.md)
is held for this image.
No offline test establishes capture, exposure, optical AF or factory parity.

Upstream 3.1 failed the A7C II check with aperture `--` and blocked shutter;
AF 3.0 failed capture/shutdown. Further trials of those images are held. The
sections below retain their historical implementation and build boundaries.


The [committed original stock 1.8.0 recovery bundle](recovery/stock-1.8.0/README.md)
includes the vendor application and an encrypted exact same-unit backup. Its
offline unpack/verification tool sends no USB reports; the key stays outside Git.

## Earlier custom firmware and metadata qualification

The first installable candidate was a **metadata qualification build with motor
motion disabled**. It uses C for the inspected SAMD21 register and E-mount paths;
it is not the production autofocus firmware or a decision against a later Rust
implementation. The macOS app and USB loader transport use native Swift.

The previous **AF 2.2 candidate** reconciles REA findings with the upstream
controller for Contax Zeiss 50mm f/1.4. The frozen **AF 2.3 candidate** adds received-
frame admission, coherent ISR snapshots, faulted Stop handling, operation
ownership, frame-paced telemetry and bounded initialization. It was installed and
USB-byte-verified after physical reconnect. The owner reports eventual loaded
50mm focus with substantial hunting; sharpness and camera qualification remain
unverified. The earlier stock 1.8.0 comparison matched its full application slot
to the original backup; the owner reported much less hunting. Camera use before
strict verification changed its saved-settings record. That historical failure
was subsequently closed by an explicit reviewed-motion resolution without
relabeling the strict failure. See the
[2.3 hardware record](../docs/evidence/af-23-upload-2026-10-11.md) and
[current stock comparison record](../docs/evidence/stock-18-comparison-2026-10-11.md).
The requested unknown-aperture behavior and current fixed-range declaration are
assessed in [manual aperture policy](../docs/manual-aperture-policy.md).
Historical custom 3.0 build and checks (these do not build upstream 3.6):

```sh
python3 scripts/build-firmware.py --variant arbitrated-af
./scripts/swift-local.sh test
python3 scripts/test-firmware.py --af
```

The custom `ea9` source builds **AF 3.0** under `ea9/build/arbitrated`, with camera BCD
0x30 and loader 3.0.0. `em_arbitration` separates capture/RX/TX/session/shutdown
ownership; `af_readiness` admits bounded nonblocking homing. Factory-derived
capture opener echo and shutdown ordering are tested against original instructions.
The preceding controller/completion/aperture/observer policies are retained.
The candidate has 392 bytes flash margin, 2,380 bytes static RAM and 8,192 bytes
reserved stack. It was prepared offline; the separately authorized October 14
upload and strict physical-reconnect readback passed, with separate offline
audits. Camera acceptance subsequently failed: half-press focus, full-press
freeze, no saved photo and battery-required recovery. Further AF 3.0 trials are
held; see [the failure investigation](../docs/evidence/af-30-camera-failure-2026-10-14.md). See [the installation record](../docs/evidence/af-30-upload-2026-10-14.md).
AF 2.9 remains held after capture freeze and battery-required recovery.
See [the 3.0 candidate](candidates/3.0.0/README.md) and
[implementation, evidence and limits](../docs/evidence/af-30-candidate-2026-10-13.md).
Factory phase scheduling, saved-origin policy, physical timing and camera
qualification remain incomplete.

The following 2.4 observations are historical. It uses a modular factory-derived controller, tested directly
against the original instructions. Its authorized upload and strict byte verification passed after physical
reconnect, including an independent audit. **Its owner focus attempt failed**:
motor response without acquisition/photo release, a dark view and no shown
f-number in P/A. Actual focus mode/exposure remain unknown. Further 2.4 camera
testing is suspended. Stock 1.8 recovery passed strict byte verification after
physical reconnect and an independent audit. A stock display/lifecycle and
matched AF-S baseline remain pending. See [the failure and controller counterexamples](../docs/evidence/af-24-camera-failure-2026-10-11.md),
[completed recovery record](../docs/evidence/stock-18-af24-recovery-2026-10-11.md)
and [historical USB record](../docs/evidence/af-24-upload-2026-10-11.md). See the [algorithm and explicit differences](../docs/reverse-engineering/factory-af-baseline.md)
and [validation record](../docs/evidence/factory-af-baseline-2026-10-11.md).
Templates/pins for 2.0–2.9 remain frozen; their build-script variants verify

Pinned custom versions remain admitted for backed-up upload, strict reconnect

See the [audit](../docs/audits/firmware-correctness-2026-10-11.md) and

See the [installation record](../docs/evidence/af-22-upload-2026-10-11.md).
The owner reported motor movement and proper A7C II shutdown with the earlier
byte-verified 2.1 image. For 2.2 the owner also reported normal startup, quiet idle and normal motor

See the [reference/timing/completion design](../docs/af-reconciliation.md),
[session evidence](../docs/evidence/af-reconciliation-2026-10-10.md),
[AF-S runbook](../docs/af-s-test.md) and

The fork is based on [weiziqian/E-mount-impl-on-Techart-EA9](https://github.com/weiziqian/E-mount-impl-on-Techart-EA9)
at commit `d52ed06cc449918f938e0695fbf29a0c4141f2b2`. The source snapshot in

retained in `ea9`; new profile and metadata-entry code uses MIT. Device headers,

Build from the repository root on Apple Silicon macOS with Python 3.12+:

```sh
python3 scripts/build-firmware.py
./scripts/swift-local.sh test
python3 scripts/test-firmware.py
./scripts/build-macos-app.sh
```

Dependency versions, official source URLs and digests are pinned in
`dependencies.json`. The local cache is ignored. The packaged Mac app includes
pinned released templates and separate fixed upstream candidates. The earlier
custom templates personalize only a reserved profile row; a custom template with
its zeroed row is intentionally invalid. Upstream 3.1–3.6 images have no runtime

- The frozen metadata release uses a dedicated `metadata_main.c` entry point; the motion implementation is not

  frame setters. No measured geometry from another lens is reused.
- Legacy adapter ID 234 and camera-reported custom firmware 2.0 are used. USB
  metadata declares 2.0.0; CHECK still runs in the original bootloader.
- Linker bounds reserve one row at `0xa000`. Startup headers/vector field names
  are adapted to DFP 2.0.4 without changing the interrupt-vector ordering.
- The inherited optical-row test now invokes the row setter explicitly; the
  new profile test proves startup retains the stock optical rows.

Use the [USB milestone procedure](../docs/usb-metadata-milestone.md) and its

startup/shutdown and timing. No autofocus claim follows from these host tests.

# Device workflow: prototype 0.19.1, build 24

Open `dist/Open LM-EA9.app`. The **Device** tab shows the adapter photo,
connection, dated firmware read and the last USB-verified lens setting.
Actual aperture is **Unknown**; the displayed fixed f-number is camera metadata.
Use the lens ring to stop down. The library editor can declare a fixed camera
f-number for firmware with a runtime profile row. Upstream candidates instead
compile the original 50mm f/1.4 profile; library edits stay local on those images.
The secondary **Lens Library** tab retains the photographs and metadata editor.

**Upstream AF 3.6.0 camera testing is held after capture and shutdown failure.**
The app shows that result and disables ordinary 3.6 installation. USB backup and
recovery remain available. [Failure and surviving diagnostic evidence](evidence/upstream-36-camera-failure-2026-10-15.md).
Do not repeat this image on the camera. Historical explicit CLI preparation/apply
commands retain their pinned images for coordinated research/recovery.

The latest packaged firmware is **upstream AF 3.6.0**.
Its [authorized upload and strict verification](evidence/upstream-36-upload-2026-10-15.md)
passed after owner-confirmed physical reconnect. The later camera trial failed;
a read-only post-camera backup and log review followed. USB tools retain the disabled
**Install Upstream AF 3.6.0** control as a separate
action; changing the dropdown does not install it. The native CLI equivalents
are `prepare-handoff-upstream` and `apply-handoff-upstream`. Other/edited profiles
are rejected. [Build/test evidence](evidence/upstream-36-handoff-2026-10-15.md)
and the [coordinated installation/camera procedure](upstream-handoff-test.md)
describe the exact image and its limits.

Startup diagnostic **3.2.0** was uploaded for the original 50mm f/1.4
profile on October 15. [Strict verification passed](evidence/upstream-32-upload-2026-10-15.md)
after owner-confirmed physical reconnect, resolving that transaction before 3.6.
Do not delete or edit a pending journal or reconnect marker.
The historical `prepare-startup`/`apply-startup`
commands still select 3.2. Installed 3.2–3.6 routes the main action to USB tools,
labels camera compatibility unqualified and avoids ordinary profile application.
After one coordinated camera cycle, save a read-only backup and use the offline
decoder for evidence review. Further 3.6 camera trials remain held.
Initial full-image verification includes the blank log area. Later log retrieval
does not relax that check; ordinary image inspection still rejects changed bytes.

AF 3.0 was prepared offline. Its October 14 upload and strict physical-reconnect
verification passed. Camera acceptance subsequently failed with full-press
freeze requiring battery removal; further AF 3.0 trials are held. See
[the failure record](evidence/af-30-camera-failure-2026-10-14.md) and
[the installation record](evidence/af-30-upload-2026-10-14.md).
AF 2.9 is explicitly held after capture/shutdown failure. See
[the historical AF 3.0 milestone](evidence/af-30-candidate-2026-10-13.md).

The [upstream 3.1 baseline](evidence/upstream-baseline-2026-10-14.md) is uploaded
and strictly byte-verified after physical reconnect, with a separate offline
audit. Camera acceptance subsequently failed: aperture `--`, blocked shutter,
no motor movement and normal shutdown. Actual focus mode remains unverified;
further 3.1 trials are held. App 0.14.1 marks that installed image as held and
disables ordinary baseline installation, retaining the verified USB history.
See [the failure investigation](evidence/upstream-31-camera-failure-2026-10-14.md) and
[the installation record](evidence/upstream-31-upload-2026-10-14.md).
App 0.14 prominently marks installed AF 3.0 as held
and routes the primary action to USB tools. Its strict USB result remains valid
while camera capture/shutdown acceptance is failed.

## Choose a lens and apply supported metadata

All eight lenses can be edited and prepared locally. **Apply profile** requires
verified firmware with a runtime profile row. The upstream 3.1–3.6 candidates
are fixed to the original 50mm f/1.4 and offer USB tools instead. They cannot
switch to the selected lens or use an aperture override without a new firmware
candidate. The following apply sequence is for supported runtime-profile images.

1. Connect the adapter through its USB cap with TECHART Update closed.
2. Choose a lens in the **Lens profile** dropdown on Device. All eight requested
   lenses are included, with the corrected Biotar 58mm f/2. The selected-on-Mac
   preview shows the focal length and reported aperture that will be applied.
3. Confirm **Updater closed · USB cap reconnected**, then click **Apply profile**.
4. After upload, physically unplug and reconnect the cap. The app detects the
   new connection; confirm the prerequisite again and click **Verify lens**.
5. Use the adapter on the camera after byte verification succeeds.

Choosing a profile saves only a local preparation. The on-adapter photo and
setting retain the last verified value until the uploaded image is verified.
An unchanged profile shows **Up to date**. The primary action preserves the
verified installed firmware variant, including legacy AF 2.1. Installing an
upstream candidate is a separate **USB tools → Experimental autofocus** action,
with its own pinned image and coordinated test. Installed fixed upstream firmware
explains its compiled configuration and offers USB tools from the dropdown.
The CLI `apply-upstream` still selects held 3.1 for explicit recovery/research;
do not retry it for camera use. Historical `apply-af` still selects held 3.0.
Plain `apply` selects metadata-only 2.0.

The status panel explains the next action: connection, one-time setup, reading
unknown settings, unsaved edits, incomplete zoom data, confirmation, reconnect,
verification or a completed profile match. If an AF version is known but its
verified lens history is missing, **Read lens settings** identifies the image
before the main profile action becomes available. It cannot silently fall back to
metadata-only firmware. A newer stock-version observation hides older AF history;
a successful stock-image read archives the old lens record and clears that setting.
An unfinished update from another adapter points to USB tools rather than offering
an unavailable verification action.

If this is a new unit, **Set up adapter** performs the existing backed-up stock
upload/reconnect qualification before custom application uploads are allowed.
The zoom requires a saved current focal length before applying; **Edit lens…**
opens its editor. Unsaved edits and unresolved update journals prevent conflicting
changes. Backups and restoration remain in USB tools.

A corrupt local firmware history now shows **Review recovery state**, hides stale
on-adapter lens information and blocks conflicting changes. The corrupt file is
retained; repairing the history is recognized on refresh. The app cannot infer
current adapter settings from an unreadable local record.

## Automatic refresh

The app checks macOS USB/HID descriptors and bounded local history every two
seconds, on launch, and when it becomes active. It detects connection changes
and reloads CLI-published verification records while the window stays open.
The monitor cancels when the view ends, skips active operations and rejects
overlapping refreshes. A changed registry ID, blocked connection or discovery
failure clears the connection acknowledgement. Multiple adapters disable USB
operations. Discovery failure clears the displayed device list.

Automatic refresh sends **no HID feature reports, CHECK, READ or START**.
Firmware and lens labels remain dated local evidence associated with the
qualified unit's serial, not fresh USB readings or identification of a passive
mounted lens. **Read Version** and **Read Adapter Lens** remain explicit in
USB tools. This distinction matters because an armed stock bootloader can
interpret an ordinary read request as the next firmware page. Keep the physical
reconnect guard even though discovery itself is automatic.

## Historical validation

The main view uses the existing sourced photos, compact adapter/firmware card,
verified lens photo and a visible dropdown/apply row. No new remote images or
runtime network requests were added. The earlier visual release was built and inspected with
the connected adapter; 0.14 packaging and tests were offline. Its last saved 2.1.0/50mm f/1.4 history loaded correctly;
the 85mm dropdown selection was exercised and restored to 50mm without an upload.
See [the test and hardware-boundary evidence](evidence/af-reconciliation-2026-10-10.md).

After the AF 2.2 reconnect/readback on Oct 11, the same app loaded the completed
2.2.0/50mm f/1.4 history and displayed **USB verified** and **Up to date** without
a rebuild or explicit HID read. See the [completed installation record](evidence/af-22-upload-2026-10-11.md).

App 0.7 and the AF 2.4 baseline were validated offline; see [the preparation evidence](evidence/factory-af-baseline-2026-10-11.md). The stock restore was subsequently resolved by an explicit reviewed-motion policy retaining its strict failure. The authorized AF 2.4 upload and strict byte verification passed after physical reconnect, with an independent audit. The later owner focus attempt failed, with a dark view and no shown f-number in P/A; further 2.4 camera trials are suspended. Stock recovery passed normal strict verification after physical reconnect and an independent audit. The new stock display/lifecycle and AF-S baseline remain pending. See [the failure investigation](evidence/af-24-camera-failure-2026-10-11.md) and [completed recovery record](evidence/stock-18-af24-recovery-2026-10-11.md).

App 0.9.0/build 12 offers explicit AF 2.6 installation. Normal dropdown changes
preserve the verified installed variant. The [2.6 record](evidence/af-26-candidate-2026-10-11.md)
covers offline preparation and the restored opaque `0x34` reply; exposure and
optical AF remain unqualified. The previous [2.5 candidate](../firmware/candidates/2.5.0/README.md)
remains frozen and held after the [aperture audit](audits/aperture-protocol-design-2026-10-11.md).
The adapter was disconnected during 2.6 preparation; that dated record describes
its own preparation boundary and does not select 2.6 in the current app.

# macOS prototype

Current app: **0.19.1, build 24**, October 15, 2026. Device opens first, with
automatic descriptor/history refresh, eight photographed lens profiles, local
metadata editing and explicit guarded USB operations. The host uses native
Swift 6, SwiftUI, selective AppKit, IOHID and CryptoKit. Firmware currently builds
on upstream C; Rust is deferred while qualifying the camera contract.

The latest packaged candidate is [upstream AF 3.6](evidence/upstream-36-handoff-2026-10-15.md),
for the original 50mm f/1.4 profile. It has no runtime profile row.
[3.2 verification passed](evidence/upstream-32-upload-2026-10-15.md) after physical
reconnect; the separately authorized [3.6 installation](evidence/upstream-36-upload-2026-10-15.md)
also passed strict verification after its own physical reconnect. The later
[3.6 camera test failed capture and shutdown](evidence/upstream-36-camera-failure-2026-10-15.md).
Post-camera logs were preserved; ordinary 3.6 installation and further camera
trials are held. See the [current Device workflow](macos-device-workflow.md)
and [coordinated 3.6 procedure](upstream-handoff-test.md). The dated
[initial prototype record](evidence/macos-prototype-2026-10-10.md) preserves the
earlier read-only milestone; current capabilities are described below.

## Build and open

From the repository root, with Xcode and its command-line tools selected:

```sh
./scripts/swift-local.sh test
./scripts/build-macos-app.sh
open "dist/Open LM-EA9.app"
```

The package declares macOS 14 as its minimum. The packaging script builds for
the current host architecture, copies the resource bundle and native icon, and
ad-hoc signs/verifies the app. This is a local development build. Developer ID,
notarization, universal distribution, clean-machine and macOS 14 qualification
remain release work. See [the validation record](evidence/macos-prototype-2026-10-10.md)
for the original backup qualification, and [Device overview validation](evidence/macos-device-overview-2026-10-10.md) for version 0.1.1.
The current [visual validation](evidence/macos-visual-redesign-2026-10-10.md)
records the gallery, local preparation, compact editor and bundled-photo checks.
On a fresh checkout, restore the Git-ignored photos first using
`python3 references/visuals/fetch_assets.py`; see [photo provenance](../references/visuals/README.md).

`swift-local.sh` puts SwiftPM/compiler caches inside `.build` and disables
SwiftPM's nested process sandbox for this dependency-free local package. It
does not give the app administrative privileges. Open `apps/macos/Package.swift`
in Xcode for source navigation/debugging. Generated `.build`, `dist` and test
artifacts are excluded from Git; application source and scripts are tracked.

## Device overview

Every launch opens **Device**. It shows the LM-EA9 connection, firmware version
and **Lens Information**. **Refresh Connection** and startup discovery inspect
macOS HID properties without sending CHECK, READ or feature reports. Discovery
errors clear the displayed device list rather than retaining a stale connected
status. The current app monitors descriptors and local history every two seconds
and when it becomes active; automatic refresh sends no HID feature reports.

Firmware begins as **Not read** until a successful explicit **Read Version**
or backup. Open **Read version…** or **USB tools…** and prepare the connection
using the prerequisite checkbox first.
Read Version uses the same exclusive session, idle acknowledgement and persisted
reconnect guard as backup, and sends exactly one qualified CHECK, with no memory
reads. Qualified stock 1.8.0 and supported pinned custom versions are accepted. This is the
loader's reported version, not an installed-image or camera-behavior check.

A dated version observation is saved privately in Application Support as
`last-firmware-observation.json`. On later launches, a matching adapter's last
read is displayed with its timestamp. It is never represented as a fresh query.
USB descriptor version is not substituted for firmware. Anonymous adapters,
different serials, unqualified descriptors, corrupt or unsupported history do
not receive a cached version. **Read Version** explicitly refreshes it; startup,
connection refresh and tab navigation never do.

The Device card shows the last USB-verified adapter setting with its date.
The Device dropdown chooses a local preparation; **Apply profile** is a separate
USB action. **Edit library…** opens the secondary Lens Library tab. A passive
mounted lens cannot be electronically identified; the stored setting describes
what the camera is told. Older prototype stages did not yet read custom metadata.

## Lens workflow

Open **Lens Library** to browse the photo grid. **Prepare lens** saves a local
choice and returns to Device; the Device dropdown now switches profiles directly. Click a
photograph or sliders button to edit metadata in a sheet, then choose **Save
Lens** (Command-S). **Revert** restores the saved values. Closing the editor or
quitting protects unsaved edits with Save/Discard/Cancel. Invalid numeric fields
show an explanation and disable Save. Editing and saving change the local library;
**Apply profile** is a separate USB action on variants with a runtime profile row.
Fixed upstream 3.1–3.6 images accept only the original unedited 50mm profile and
route other selections to USB tools rather than silently changing firmware.

The first launch seeds the library from the canonical
[requested inventory](../profiles/requested-lenses.json). A bundled copy is
checked against that file when packaging. Subsequent launches open the local
library rather than resetting it. All eight profiles retain their original
IDs and user-supplied names, including the 28–70 mm zoom. The Biotar is now
58 mm f/2 as confirmed by the owner; its legacy `zeiss-jena-biotar-55-f2` ID is
retained. Existing saved libraries are never silently reset. The macro's
calibration note is retained. **Photo Credits…** shows photo sources and variants.

For a zoom, enter a minimum, maximum and optional current focal length. Leave
the current setting blank if unknown. Nominal maximum aperture is a lens
specification; the optional fixed camera f-number is owner-declared metadata.
The physical iris remains **Unknown** even when that field is set. Use the lens
ring to stop down; the passive mount does not sense its setting. Calibration
remains explicitly unmeasured. The zoom's variable-aperture table, optical
model, camera-facing lens ID and focus-reference calibration are not invented.

The app saves to:

```text
~/Library/Application Support/org.openlmea9.prototype/profiles.json
```

The separate `prepared-lens.json` records only the locally chosen profile ID.
Neither file represents adapter configuration.

**Export saved library** in the library options or File menu writes versioned JSON using the native save panel.
Unsaved edits are excluded. **Import** validates and previews the profile
count/camera, then asks before replacing the local library. It preserves a
`profiles-before-import-<UUID>.json` copy of the prior file. Save current edits
or revert them before importing. An unreadable or newer-schema local file is
preserved, saving is disabled, and a valid import provides explicit recovery.

For development/UI checks, launch an isolated library:

```sh
open -n "dist/Open LM-EA9.app" --args --library-directory /tmp/ea9-ui-library
```

## USB backup workflow

Open **Device → USB tools…**, choose **Refresh Connection**, and expand
**Read-only USB backup**. Discovery sends no reports. Backup requires exactly one device
with the qualified descriptor. Close the official updater and other USB tools,
physically unplug/reconnect the USB cap, refresh, and check the prerequisite
box. Choose **Create Verified Backup…** and a new `.ea9backup` name.

The reconnect prerequisite is substantive: the stock loader treats reports as
flash data when an update session is already armed. Even a CHECK could then be
consumed as data. This app cannot determine that state without sending a
report. Exclusive access prevents concurrent host owners during explicit USB reads but
cannot clear a previously armed loader. See the
[measured investigation](usb-cap-investigation.md).

The backup qualifies the known CHECK response and bootloader code, confirms
chip/flash capacity, compares two complete main-flash reads and two reads each
of the user-fuse/calibration windows, then verifies the written files. Progress
and cancellation stay off the HID worker. Success publishes one private
package with a manifest and SHA-256 checksums. **Show in Finder** reveals it.
Existing backups are never overwritten. Failed/cancelled reads publish no
partial package.

After an uncertain exchange, cancellation, crash or interrupted session,
physically reconnect and refresh. The connection's registry ID is persisted in
`usb-reconnect-required.json` before the transaction and cleared on successful
completion. Relaunching the app does not bypass this guard. Conservative open
failures may also require reconnect. There are no automatic transport retries.
Descriptor/history refresh also runs every two seconds and on app activation;
automatic refresh sends no CHECK, READ, START or feature reports.

The package includes device serial/unit data. It is private local evidence,
with a `0700` directory and `0600` files. The app sends nothing to a server.
Complete flash read-back and the same-unit application upload/restoration path
have been exercised with physical reconnect and strict byte comparison.
Bootloader restoration and power-loss recovery remain unqualified. Other factory
auxiliary rows and unique-ID words are outside this backup. USB tools expose
pinned application installation, verification and stock application restoration;
they provide no arbitrary memory writer or direct motor command.

## Command-line diagnostics

The packaged CLI uses the same DeviceKit pipeline as the GUI:

```sh
./dist/ea9ctl inventory
./dist/ea9ctl backup /path/to/new-backup.ea9backup --idle
```

`--idle` acknowledges the same closed-updater/physical-reconnect prerequisite.
Inventory prints a redacted summary and sends no reports. Backup prints only
the destination, size, flash digest and exchange count. The manifest retains
private identity. `--state-directory PATH` selects library and history storage;
the physical reconnect guard and USB operation lock always remain in canonical
Application Support state. This flag cannot bypass an armed connection. Use the
shared default for coordinated hardware operations and run one USB client at a time.

Verify a saved package later without USB access:

```sh
python3 tools/verify_macos_backup.py /path/to/backup.ea9backup
```

This checks file sizes/hashes, the loader digest, chip/geometry and recorded
scope/counts. It does not independently prove the manifest's claimed hardware
read history or authenticate its creator.

## Module boundaries and future work

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `LensCore` | Seed inventory, metadata validation, versioned local JSON, atomic saves/import preservation |
| `DeviceKit/Backup` | Closed CHECK/READ codec, qualification, read comparison, manifest and atomic package publication |
| `DeviceKit/FirmwareObservation` | Dated device-reported version, bounded private history, response qualification |
| `DeviceKit/NativeHID` | Descriptor discovery, exclusive session, owned run loop/callback buffers, deadline/cancellation/reconnect handling |
| `DeviceKit/Upload` | Pinned application reports, durable journal, strict reconnect verification and protected-data comparison |
| `OpenLMEA9` | SwiftUI presentation, AppKit file panels/quit handling, draft versus saved state |
| `EA9CLI` | Headless access to the same guarded backup, upload and verification services |

The device service reserves the entire operation using a lock, runs all native
HID lifetime operations on one worker thread, and returns Sendable value types.
It does not rely on actor isolation across `await` to serialize a transaction.
Read reports use a closed read-only request enum; upload START/pages use a
separate report type. After START, the connection is blocked until physical
reconnect; no CHECK, READ, end marker, retry or extra padding follows it. Callback data
is copied before the next report; mismatched type, ID, length, duplicate input,
unsolicited input or deadline failure stops the session. Swift's two
`@unchecked Sendable` classes are the cancellation token and device service;
their mutable cross-thread state is lock protected. Native objects/pointers
never cross into SwiftUI.

This prototype chooses the audit's pure Swift host alternative: shared Rust
code would currently add an FFI/build boundary without a firmware contract to
share. A future pure Rust codec can replace a bounded internal codec after
the firmware/management schemas earn that reuse. The Mac transport remains
native. The app is prepared for a separate management backend; stock backup
access does not establish application USB reachability or autofocus quality.

Next qualification includes an application management service without reflashing,
body-specific capture/exposure/optical/motion tests,
sleep/unplug stress and full VoiceOver/keyboard testing on supported OS builds.
See [system design](system-design-recommendation.md) and the separate
[profile/backup format contract](macos-prototype-formats.md).

Primary implementation sources: Apple's local SDK
`IOKit.framework/Headers/hid/IOHIDDevice.h` (exclusive opening, callback and
run-loop lifetime) and
[IOHIDDeviceSetReport](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/iokit/1588656-iohiddevicesetreport);
[Swift PackageDescription](https://docs.swift.org/package-manager/PackageDescription/PackageDescription.html).
Hardware behavior comes from the pinned local bootloader analysis and measured
USB evidence, rather than generic USB API documentation.


## Historical experimental AF milestone (0.4.0, build 7)

USB tools now includes an **Experimental autofocus** disclosure with explicit AF
and metadata-only installation actions. Both save a recovery backup, use pinned
images and require physical reconnect plus byte verification. AF uses 2.1.0;
metadata-only remains 2.0.0. Ordinary lens changes preserve verified AF capability.
An unknown/unverified firmware state does not imply that motor movement is disabled.
The landing page and secondary Lens Library retain their existing visual layout.
See [the 50mm AF-S runbook](af-s-test.md) for the first physical test and restoration.
No AF hardware upload or camera qualification occurred while building this version.

# Recommended LM-EA9 system design

## Updated working recommendation — October 15, 2026

The owner subsequently authorized the upstream C direction for the
[3.2 startup/handshake milestone](evidence/upstream-32-startup-diagnostic-2026-10-15.md).
That image was uploaded and [strictly verified](evidence/upstream-32-upload-2026-10-15.md)
after owner-confirmed physical reconnect. The [October 15 hardening campaign](firmware-hardening-2026-10-15.md)
then prepared separately versioned offline candidates with reproduced software
fault fixes, most recently [3.6](evidence/upstream-36-handoff-2026-10-15.md).
App 0.19/build 23 introduced its separate explicit installation action;
current app0.19.1/build24 disables that ordinary action after the reported failure.
Its [owner-authorized 3.6 installation](evidence/upstream-36-upload-2026-10-15.md)
passed strict verification after its own physical reconnect. The later
[camera trial failed capture/shutdown](evidence/upstream-36-camera-failure-2026-10-15.md),
and a read-only backup preserved diagnostic evidence. Further 3.6 trials are held.
They retain the upstream controller and native Swift host;
A7C II acceptance remains unqualified. This source hardening does not replace
the outstanding initial camera qualification gate.

Use the pinned upstream **C firmware as the development foundation**, retain the
native SwiftUI/AppKit application and Swift IOHID/update service, and keep the
management contract independent of language. Defer a Rust firmware port and a
shared Rust host core until there is a camera-qualified baseline and a concrete
benefit to justify the added boundaries. Every firmware candidate flashed in
this project has been C; Rust is not implicated in these failures.

This recommendation answers the owner's question about adopting upstream
instead of continuing the Rust plan. It does not claim upstream is qualified:
the direct 3.1 build also failed this A7C II check, showing aperture `--` and a
blocked shutter with normal shutdown. See [the failure and five-case startup
investigation](evidence/upstream-31-camera-failure-2026-10-14.md).

The next firmware milestone is startup/handshake, nominal lens information,
MF capture and shutdown on this body, then bounded AF-S and saved-photo checks.
Only after that baseline succeeds should metadata persistence or controller
changes be added, one independently testable step at a time. Preserve the
factory REA findings and previous modular work as comparison evidence; do not
merge reconstructed behavior wholesale into the first baseline. Keep the
existing backed-up native upload/reconnect/verification service rather than
replacing it with an unreviewed flashing path. No new image or flash follows
from this recommendation alone.

The sections below retain the **earlier October 10 Rust-first research
recommendation and its qualification gates**, rather than the current working
direction above.

> Historical follow-up (prototype 0.3.0): the [USB metadata milestone](usb-metadata-milestone.md) added a reviewed, bounded application upload, mandatory physical reconnect and full byte verification. Its first firmware candidate used the reference C implementation with motor motion disabled. [Actual measurements](evidence/usb-metadata-milestone-2026-10-10.md) distinguish stock upload qualification, custom read-back and pending camera checks. The material below records the earlier research/prototype stage.

Implementation follow-up: the user authorized the
[native Mac prototype](macos-prototype.md), now using SwiftUI/AppKit, native Swift
IOHID, local metadata and verified read-only backup. The current host core is
pure Swift because a shared Rust codec has no established firmware contract to
reuse yet. This adopts the recommended host direction without freezing the
production firmware language or management-service design.

October 10, 2026. Synthesis of three parallel audits:
[firmware](audits/firmware-options.md),
[host protocol](audits/host-protocol-options.md), and
[macOS](audits/macos-options.md). The requirements remain in
[product-direction.md](product-direction.md).

Follow-up: the [connected-device USB-cap investigation](usb-cap-investigation.md)
now confirms native macOS CHECK/READ and the installed 1.8.0 application. It also
finds that the stock bootloader's USB mode stays in the bootloader, with no
supported application-launch path in its inspected handlers. Application
management needs a qualified entry bridge or alternate cap/mode arrangement.

The [read-only follow-up](usb-cap-followup.md) now measures ATSAMD21E17A revision
D, 128 KiB flash, clear security/boot protection and unlocked regions. Two full
flash backups match; PA23 reads high as an input with a pull-down in cap mode.
Independent recovery and physical electrical checks remain pending. The
[entry proposal](management-entry-design.md) favors a small launch extension
after recovery qualification and records the handoff requirements.

The user subsequently reported an unplug event and USB-only access. A matching
device re-enumerated with a new registry entry; a complete flash read and the
qualified snapshots still match. Continue host/offline firmware prototypes
within the [USB-only boundary](usb-only-next-steps.md); independent restoration
and electrical measurements remain unqualified.

## Recommended direction

**Prototype Rust `no_std` firmware, a native SwiftUI/AppKit macOS app, and a
language-neutral management protocol.** Use a small shared Rust library for
pure codecs and validation if that reuse earns its integration cost. Swift
owns the OS device connection and application lifecycle. Preserve the original
bootloader and retain modular C as the firmware fallback.

This is the preferred design to qualify, not a declaration that the research
or hardware validation is complete. Select the production stack after the
prototype gates below. No adapter was accessed, toolchain installed, updater
executed, or firmware flashed during these audits.

| Layer | Recommendation | Reason and qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Firmware language | Rust `no_std`; C fallback | Strong fit for validated parsing and explicit state/ownership; complete EA9 memory/timing still unproven. C has the collected working hardware reference. |
| Scheduling | Short interrupts, periodic motion step, bounded event/state machines | Matches small MCU and camera timing; keep a runtime upgrade optional. |
| Hardware boundary | Small EA9 board package using a pinned PAC/HAL and audited register operations | Preserve actual pin/clock/output behavior; generic board defaults are unsuitable. |
| Host management contract | Versioned bounded binary envelope, restricted CBOR payloads and CDDL schema | Independent of implementation language; TLV remains the footprint fallback. |
| Host connection | Native Swift IOHID adapter, initially the existing bootloader protocol | Small platform boundary with explicit report and session ownership. |
| Application USB service | Vendor HID, conditional on a qualified entry bridge or alternate cap/mode path | Suitable for small settings/diagnostic messages; the inspected stock USB boot path does not launch the application. |
| macOS UI | SwiftUI with selective AppKit | Best current fit for native Mac interaction, file workflows and accessibility. |
| Shared host/device logic | Narrow synchronous Rust codec/profile/image library, conditional on demonstrated benefit | Avoid inconsistent validation while containing FFI and concurrency complexity. |
| Configuration | Image-embedded profile bundle first; transactional persistent banks when supported | Fits the evidenced uploader; dedicated writes need a proven service and erase boundaries. |
| Updates | Recognized release package, stock bootloader, backup and complete read-back | Keeps the existing recovery channel; no unsupported rollback/resume promise. |

Rust's official target covers Cortex-M0+ bare-metal execution; the atsamd-rs
project supplies SAMD21 support. Neither establishes a working EA9 build.
[Rust target](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/platform-support/thumbv6m-none-eabi.html),
[atsamd-rs](https://github.com/atsamd-rs/atsamd).
The native UI judgment follows the Mac-only product goal, rather than a
single-language preference. SwiftUI can integrate AppKit views through
[NSViewRepresentable](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/nsviewrepresentable).

## Architecture and ownership

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Mac[macOS application]
        UI[SwiftUI and selective AppKit]
        Model[Lens library and confirmed device state]
        Ops[Swift device session and operation coordinator]
        Core[Pure codecs, profile and image validation]
        HID[Native IOHID transport]
        UI --> Model
        Model --> Ops
        Ops <--> Core
        Ops --> HID
    end
    HID --> Legacy[Stock bootloader: read and install]
    Legacy --> Image[Custom application image and profile bundle]
    HID -. conditional application access .-> Mgmt[Management service]
    subgraph Device[LM-EA9 application]
        Session[E-mount session and frame codec]
        Supervisor[Lifecycle and motion supervisor]
        Axis[Trajectory, servo and position estimator]
        Board[Board: UART, encoder, PWM, clocks]
        Profiles[Profiles and unit calibration]
        Store[Configuration and bounded diagnostics]
        Mgmt --> Supervisor
        Mgmt <--> Store
        Store --> Profiles
        Profiles --> Session
        Profiles --> Axis
        Session <--> Supervisor
        Supervisor --> Axis
        Axis <--> Board
        Session <--> Board
    end
    Camera[Sony A7C II] <--> Session
    Image --> Profiles
    Core -. common pure implementation if qualified .-> Session
```

The diagram's dashed USB path is a proposed capability. Stock bootloader CHECK
and READ have now been repeated on the user's device; installation and an
application USB service have not. Camera and USB-cap sessions should be separate
until hardware evidence demonstrates otherwise.

One module owns each resource. The board package owns peripheral access. The
motion axis owns motor commands. The lifecycle supervisor admits or rejects
camera/management requests according to operating mode. The camera session owns
protocol completion events; it reports arrival from motion evidence, not from
having queued a command. Activate a profile as a consistent validated snapshot,
so status messages and the controller cannot use different lens descriptions.

Keep the E-mount codec, focus models, profile validation, management schema and
configuration-record logic independent of register code. Test them on the Mac
using the same wire vectors whether the final implementation is Rust or C.
Isolate firmware `unsafe`, DMA/interrupt handoffs and any FFI within small
reviewable boundaries.

## Firmware execution and autofocus

The reference targets 48 MHz SAMD21E17A with 128 KiB flash and 16 KiB SRAM.
The application starts at `0x5000`, leaving 108 KiB above the bootloader before
configuration/log reservations. Confirm this physical unit rather than using
a larger development-board map. Its replacement firmware uses **SysTick** for
milliseconds; the earlier TC4 summary has been corrected.
[Reference linker](../references/upstream/weiziqian/E-mount-impl-on-Techart-EA9/src/ea9.ld),
[delay implementation](../references/upstream/weiziqian/E-mount-impl-on-Techart-EA9/src/delay.c).

Start with the reference's 750 kbaud transport and 5 ms control cadence, then
measure timing on the unit. A UART byte occupies about 13.33 microseconds;
210 bytes take 2.8 ms on the wire. Those are transmission times, not execution
measurements. Capture CS/VD edges, use bounded RX buffers with explicit overflow
handling, validate length/checksum/terminator, and separate trailing window
bytes before interpreting commands. Consider interrupt-driven TX or DMA when
polling materially affects measured control jitter. Last-byte UART completion
and CS release timing remain explicit responsibilities.

Use state machines for startup, homing, ready, motion, scan/drive, stopping,
parking, management and fault handling. Specify abort priority, relative-command
ordering, retargeting and event semantics; a single latest-target variable does
not preserve every command. Every ISR and dispatcher step has bounded work.
Choose a general executor or RTOS only when a demonstrated concurrency need
justifies its RAM and timing cost. RTIC, Embassy and statically allocated
FreeRTOS are viable alternatives, not unsupported technologies.

Measure encoder scale/polarity/noise, load-dependent drive response, friction,
stopping distance, relaxation, travel and fault behavior. Keep motor-off fault
handling and watchdog/reset behavior board-validated. An endless panic/default
handler must not leave PWM running. Use a bounded RAM trace, dropped-record
counters and controlled persistent fault records; avoid routine frame-by-frame
flash logging.

The Sony body performs image-based focus estimation and issues requests. Our
firmware's autofocus quality comes from correct camera dialogue, motion,
completion reports, calibration and consistent optical descriptions. Metadata,
optical calibration and unit-specific mechanism calibration are separate records
with provenance. Unknown calibration stays unknown. Zoom, manual aperture and
prefocus settings cannot be discovered through the passive adapter.

## Host protocol and persistence

Maintain three separate specifications: Sony E-mount semantics, the existing
bootloader exchange, and our versioned management contract. Firmware version,
protocol version, schema revision, installed image digest, profile generation
and camera-facing identity are distinct fields.

For management messages, specify a fixed envelope with version, operation,
session/request identity, bounded length, integrity and bounded fragmentation.
Prefer a restricted CBOR profile: explicit integer units and keys, bounded text
and bytes, shallow arrays/maps, definite lengths, no duplicate keys or unsupported
tags/floats. CDDL and golden vectors own the contract; language struct layouts
do not. Measure its target codec against minimal TLV before freezing encoding
and size limits. [CBOR](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8949.html),
[CDDL](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc8610/).

Operations should cover identity/capabilities, current state, bounded library
reads, begin/write/validate/commit/abort/query configuration transactions,
profile selection, diagnostics and update coordination. Mutations carry an
expected generation and explicit transaction identity. Duplicate chunks/commit
requests must be idempotent; after a lost response, query committed state rather
than assume failure. Capability discovery must accurately distinguish legacy
apply-by-image from dedicated settings writes.

**Application USB entry is the central architecture gate.** The actual
bootloader's PA23-high USB branch remains in an infinite loop; the inspected
report/control handlers provide no supported application-launch path. Native
CHECK and READ work, but a USB driver in the application cannot bypass this
entry barrier. See [the investigation](usb-cap-investigation.md). Qualify cap
wiring/mode alternatives or a minimal launch bridge before promising that
endpoint. A bootloader extension needs its own recovery evidence and explicit
scope; it has not been adopted or implemented here.

The first supported integration can personalize a recognized custom release's
reserved profile section and upload it. This requires no compiler on the user's
Mac. Preload a compact catalog for the supplied lenses where capacity allows;
test any camera control sequence for selecting profiles as a separate A7C II
feature. Do not claim a RAM selection persists after power loss unless it does.

When dedicated writes become reachable, use row-aligned A/B configuration banks,
generation/length/CRC, and a separately written commit record. Validate and
read back the inactive bank before committing; retain the previous valid bank.
Validate power cuts at every erase/program boundary. Reserve code, config,
selection journal, logs and `.noinit` state explicitly in the linker. Freeze
addresses only after measuring profile sizes and the bootloader's entire erase/
write footprint. Main-array flash stalls make persistence during camera/motor
deadlines unsuitable without additional measured evidence.

Configuration commit behavior and firmware installation are different guarantees.
The stock loader streams an application without on-device atomic swap, demonstrated
resume or rollback. The pinned uploader's inclusive loop sends `limit + 64`
bytes; for the 20,172-byte stock image that is a calculated 20,544-byte span,
conditionally `[0x5000, 0xA040)`. Confirm actual transfer/erase behavior before
depending on any supposedly preserved partition.
[Uploader](../references/upstream/weiziqian/E-mount-impl-on-Techart-EA9/tools/ea9flash.py).

## macOS app and shared core

Build native presentation and a Swift device-operation layer. Keep a dedicated
IOHID callback/queue boundary, copy report data into owned buffers, and normalize
report IDs once. Swift owns discovery, device selection, open/close, hotplug,
timeouts, sleep/wake and reconnect generations. A Rust shared library initially
handles synchronous pure functions only: profiles, wire bytes and image/config
validation. Test its ownership/error/panic boundary and required architecture
slices before adding broader bindings. Avoid duplicate Swift and Rust transport
owners.

Reserve an **entire device transaction**, not just individual report calls.
Swift actors can interleave work at `await`, so actor isolation alone does not
serialize CHECK/READ/install sessions. Legacy READ responses do not echo an
address and upload ACKs have no chunk sequence; an ambiguous timeout requires
tested resynchronization rather than blind retries.
[Swift actor semantics](https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolution/blob/main/proposals/0306-actors.md).

Use a conventional Lens Library, Device and Diagnostics layout. Normal users
choose a lens, edit known metadata, connect in the supported mode, apply and
see a meaningful result. The zoom gets explicit active focal length; the macro
gets a manual reference setting. Keep optical tables/controller tuning in
advanced views. The app distinguishes saved locally, pending, read back, and
camera-validated state without exposing wire details to ordinary users.

Store versioned local profile documents with atomic file replacement, explicit
IDs/revisions, import/export and migrations. Backups and diagnostic evidence
have their own store. A cloud service or database is not needed for the current
small personal lens library. Provide keyboard/VoiceOver paths and readable
diagnostic summaries alongside plots.

Prefer direct distribution of a signed/notarized app; choose the minimum macOS
version and distribution channel before packaging prototypes. Validate USB
access on the intended signed build. Release packages should bind hardware
compatibility, code identity, config location/schema and permitted upload span.
The host should verify artifact origin and the personalized image, then compare
installed bytes. Host signature verification does not add secure boot to the
retained loader.

## Alternatives and decision rules

| Alternative | When it would become preferable |
| --- | --- |
| Modular C firmware | Rust fails actual resource/timing/driver/debug gates or requires substantially more custom infrastructure. Interfaces and fixtures remain the same. |
| Restrained C++ firmware | Strong team expertise and a demonstrated abstraction/maintenance gain over C or Rust. |
| RTIC / Embassy | Measured coordination benefit with acceptable lock/poll latency and memory use. |
| FreeRTOS / Zephyr | A concrete feature requires their services and the complete board build fits deadlines/memory. |
| Pure Swift host core | Shared Rust adds more build/FFI maintenance than useful validation reuse. |
| egui/eframe | Cross-platform or engineering-tool needs dominate and an actual Mac accessibility/interaction prototype passes. |
| Tauri | Web UI expertise/reuse or broader platform delivery becomes a requirement worth the additional web/native boundary. |
| Qt | Team expertise or cross-platform desktop needs justify framework deployment and module licensing. |
| TLV / Protobuf | TLV wins measured footprint/simplicity, or Protobuf tooling materially simplifies the maintained cross-language contract. |
| CDC / bulk USB | Measured debugging or trace-throughput needs justify another application transport, after reachability is proved. |

The audits include broader options and why managed embedded runtimes, generic
RPC stacks, filesystem-based settings and a new bootloader are not leading
choices for the evidenced requirements. These are practical rankings, not
language/toolkit performance measurements.

## Next work and production selection gates

1. **Read-only hardware evidence, partly complete:** descriptors, CHECK, exact
   chip/capacity/protection, user fuses/calibration and complete main-flash
   backups are captured. A full read and qualified snapshots after the reported
   unplug/re-enumeration match. Still establish cap wiring/levels, independent
   recovery, and stock A7C II traffic/focus results. Current equipment is USB
   only; reset/supply timing was not instrumented.
2. **Offline shared contracts:** replay all 3,456 validated historical frames,
   corrupted/truncated/tail cases and management/config vectors. Define profile
   schema, release-image format and version/capability rules independently of
   the selected language.
3. **Comparable firmware prototypes:** minimal C and Rust builds with correct
   vectors/board map, then motor-disabled handshake. Measure full linked flash,
   RAM/stack, ISR masking, UART loss, CS timing, control jitter and fault paths.
   A proposed initial gate is at least 25% SRAM headroom after worst-case stack;
   report this as a target, not an existing result.
4. **Native app prototype:** offline editor and scripted fake transport, followed
   by a read-only IOHID build. Test transaction exclusivity, unplug/late reports,
   keyboard/VoiceOver, signing and clean-machine operation. Qualify narrow FFI
   only if it pays for itself.
5. **Configuration-access decision:** qualify an application entry bridge or
   alternate cap/mode path against the stock bootloader barrier, establish
   erase/padding behavior, then choose the settings backend. Perform simulated
   and controlled power-loss tests before advertising transactions.
6. **Motion and optics:** supervised bounded movement, then the 50 mm prime,
   repeated center/edge/distance tests, other lenses, macro/zoom workflow, AF-C
   and tracking. Video support requires separate evidence. Compare image results
   and faults, not just apparent motor speed.
7. **Record the production decision:** select Rust if its complete prototype
   meets the gates; otherwise choose modular C. Finalize transport/schema
   bindings and partitions from measurements, then implement/package the product.

The architecture can be adopted as the design direction now. The stack,
on-device USB service, persistence guarantees and compatibility claims become
production commitments only when their evidence passes these gates.

# 3.6.0 — upstream C startup handoff, Contax Zeiss 50mm f/1.4

**Camera acceptance failed; further trials are held.** Upload and strict
verification passed; the owner then reported shutter-press freeze and shutdown
nonresponse. [Failure and surviving logs](../../../docs/evidence/upstream-36-camera-failure-2026-10-15.md).
App0.19.1/build24 disables ordinary installation. The image, manifest and patch
below remain unchanged.

The original offline preparation extends frozen
[3.5](../3.5.0/README.md) with a scoped startup receive-ownership fix.
It retains the upstream controller, gains, optical tables, aperture policy,
motor/sensor drivers, wait budgets and diagnostic storage.
[Unified evidence](../../../docs/evidence/upstream-36-handoff-2026-10-15.md).

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Loader / camera version | 3.6.0 / BCD `0x36` |
| Image | 20,480 bytes, `[0x5000,0xa000)` |
| SHA-256 | `d8a60e48484d1b48e3aff0da18e6d89453d1284a8b23dca01393b320fdc6651f` |
| Code/data end / margin before logs | `0x9af4` / 268 bytes |
| Diagnostic storage | `[0x9c00,0xa000)`, sixteen append-only 64-byte pages; no runtime erase |
| Static RAM / reserved stack | 3,064 / 8,192 bytes |
| Conditional compiled stack envelope | 1,560 bytes; physical high-water unmeasured |
| Lens / nominal aperture | Original fixed 50mm f/1.4 profile; lens ID 234, AV 4352 |
| Physical iris / runtime profiles | Actual aperture Unknown; no runtime profile row |

Startup previously enabled EIC interrupts before calling the falling-edge
receive path in foreground to rescue the first window. A rising EIC interrupt
could reset the buffer during that copy. The new EIC setup/start boundary defers
only EIC delivery until rescue/reset finishes. UART and SysTick remain live;
PRIMASK is unchanged and pending EIC state is retained. A global interrupt-mask
proposal was rejected because it could delay a final UART byte past rescue.

Two legacy-only RAM snapshots of the live RX byte counter are omitted under
`EA9_NO_LOG`; their only readers are excluded logging pages. The live counter,
MMIO, emitted frames and startup diagnostics remain active. ARM preprocessing
and complete synthetic trace/wire comparisons verify that scope. This retains
the established 256-byte flash-margin floor without shortening logs or waits.

Independent tests cover 287 asserted cases, including 41 against exact final
3.6 source and failing controls. The compiled review verifies EIC disable,
barriers, rescue/reset, then enable, with 29 negative evidence controls. Repeat
builds and the unified firmware/decoder checks pass; all 53 Swift tests pass.
These contracts do not qualify peripheral timing, exposure, capture, shutdown
or optical AF. Edge coalescing and receive-boundary limits remain documented.

App **0.19.0/build 23** offers **USB tools → Install Upstream AF 3.6.0**.
Explicit commands: `prepare-handoff-upstream` / `apply-handoff-upstream`.
Earlier commands retain their images. Only the original unedited 50mm profile
is supported. Actual iris stays Unknown; factory reconstruction remains partial.

The prior 3.2 transaction and this 3.6 installation passed strict verification
after separate owner-confirmed physical reconnects. Camera failure does not
invalidate those byte comparisons. Do not repeat 3.6 trials. See the
[held coordinated procedure](../../../docs/upstream-handoff-test.md),
[build/test workbench](../../upstream-hardening/next36/README.md),
[manifest](contax-zeiss-50-f1-4.manifest.json) and
